title: The Brahmin's Petition Is Fulfilled and Dileramian Opens

blocks.text: After three days of ransacking Kasur, the narrative returns to the grievance that first set the expedition in motion. The Brahmin appears again before the chiefs, Reminding the Khalsa about his wife's captivity under the Pathans and forcing them to prove that the campaign will answer the original wrong rather than vanish into general loot.

Hari Singh directs the matter into a formal and then practical resolution. Guided by the Brahmin to the responsible house, the Khalsa kills the abductors and restores the woman, completing the justice claim that had justified the march on Kasur in the first place.

Before the page ends, however, the poem pivots to a fresh concern and opens the Dileramian episode. The Kasur campaign closes on fulfilled petition, and a new political-financial narrative begins immediately after it.
